title: Early soybean yield estimation
description: Python pipeline that combines satellite data, weather, and official yields to estimate the soybean campaign months before harvest.

caseStudy.problem: Knowing how the soybean campaign is shaping up in northwestern Buenos Aires province months before harvest, using only public data.
caseStudy.approach: A reusable Python pipeline that combines satellite NDVI (MODIS via Google Earth Engine), weather (NASA POWER), and official yields (MAGyP) for 5 counties and 25 campaigns. Random Forest with walk-forward temporal validation and SHAP interpretability. I tried other algorithms (Ridge, Lasso, XGBoost, SVR, KNN) and crop masks: none beat the base model.
caseStudy.result: With data through January (≈3 months before harvest), a mean error of ~3.3 qq/ha (R² ≈ 0.54) and 71% accuracy on the direction of the campaign. Public dashboard that updates with every push.
caseStudy.learnings: The ceiling is the data, not the algorithm; validate over time instead of fitting to the test; document the errors you find (I found and fixed an error in the satellite data that was inflating the results).
